title: Transferability Rule
description:
What must happen, to which artifacts, under which envelope conditions.
- `appliesTo` — the artifacts this rule governs, by `id`. Omit it for a rule about the workflow
  as a whole.
- `when` — the conditions, each citing an envelope constraint by `id` and how the target is
  tested against it (`inside`/`outside`). **Conjunctive: all of them must hold.** A disjunction
  is written as two rules.
- `actions` — an **OR-set**: any one resolves the rule. Never a sequence, never a combination to
  apply together.
- `mandatory` — whether applying one is required once the conditions hold.
**`when` is what makes a rule evaluable rather than merely readable.** `triggeredBy: different-geographic-coverage` is a string a person reads; `when: [{constraint: clms-coverage, test: outside}]` names the boundary, and if that constraint's dimension is spatial its value is a `geo:asWKT` geometry, so a GeoSPARQL engine can settle the question with `geof:sfWithin`. Where the cited constraint is prose-valued (a comparable ecological range), the same structure records a judgement a person still has to make — which is honest about where automation stops rather than pretending the whole model is machine-decidable.
`triggeredBy` is kept, but optional: not every evidenced FOCAL case has a constraint precise enough to cite, and forcing one would mean inventing boundaries. At least one of `when` or `triggeredBy` is required, so no rule is left with no stated condition at all. Prefer `when`.

appliesTo.description: Identifiers of the artifacts this rule governs, from the enclosing statement's `artifacts`. Several artifacts may share one rule — FP-WF2's four Czechia-specific reference files do. Omit for a rule that applies to the workflow as a whole.

when.description: The conditions under which this rule fires, ANDed together. Two conditions here mean both must hold; two rules mean either suffices.

triggeredBy.description: A coarse statement of what fires this rule, for cases where no envelope constraint can be cited precisely. Open vocabulary — see bblocks://ogc.focal.transferability.vocab.

actions.description: One or more actions, any of which resolves the rule — an OR-set, not a required combination. No evidenced case needs two applied simultaneously.

mandatory.description:
Whether applying one of `actions` is mandatory once the conditions hold. Defaults to true. When false, skipping is allowed but degrades result quality or trust rather than blocking execution — say what degrades in `transferabilityNotes`.
Named `mandatory` rather than `required`: a data property spelled like a JSON Schema keyword reads as the keyword, and this one sits beside real `required` lists.

constraint.description: The `id` of an envelope constraint in the enclosing statement's `envelope`.

test.description: How the target is compared against that constraint. `outside` is the condition under which almost every evidenced FOCAL rule fires; `inside` states the complementary case, which is what lets a cascade be written without losing its connecting condition — UP-WF2's "reuse within the domain, otherwise substitute or fail" is two rules over the same constraint. Open vocabulary — see bblocks://ogc.focal.transferability.vocab, where each term also records how it is evaluated per dimension.
